result.note: Tests the auto PLI outcomes, the ACC battery PLI's outlay, allocations and incentive claims, and its installed capacity as of February 2026.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) batteries, as updated to Parliament in July 2026:
items: It has a budget of INR 18,100 crore and targets 50 GWh of domestic capacity.
Four firms hold capacity allocations totalling 40 GWh.
Two of the beneficiary firms have already claimed incentives under the scheme.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because none of the four firms has claimed an incentive, since payouts require the production and sale of qualifying Indian-made cells. Beneficiaries reported only INR 5,180 crore of investment by May 31, 2026, against the INR 45,000 crore originally envisaged.
questions.source: Four firms hold allocations totalling 40 GWh, but none has claimed an incentive, which requires the production and sale of qualifying Indian-made cells.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, the government updated Parliament on the PLI scheme for automobiles and auto components. Consider the following pairs:
items: Units across which incentives were disbursed — 225
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: All three pairs match the figures given to Parliament. Manufacturers had also invested INR 44,326 crore, and the government had disbursed INR 2,386 crore in incentives.
questions.source: The government has disbursed INR 2,386 crore (USD 248 million) in incentives across 225 units.

questions.prompt: According to a February 2026 update, how much installed capacity had been set up under the PLI scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries?
questions.explain: The February 2026 update reported just 1 GWh of installed capacity, all of it belonging to Ola. Beneficiaries had been given two years to set up factories when capacity was awarded in March 2022, against a scheme target of 50 GWh.
questions.source: A February 2026 update reported just 1 GWh of installed capacity, entirely belonging to Ola.
